query: Weird one: `nc -zv 127.0.0.1 27018` reports the port is open and succeeds, so I assumed the tunnel is healthy, but Compass connects and then just hangs with no data coming back. If the port is open, why isn't it working?
expected_behavior: Explains that nc success only proves TCP is open, NOT that MongoDB is answering
Identifies the likely cause: a zombie SSH session — the local port stays forwarded but the far end is dead
Recommends testing at the MongoDB wire-protocol level instead, e.g. mongosh ... --eval 'db.runCommand({ping:1})'
Recommends killing and re-establishing the tunnel (pkill -f "ssh.*-L <port>")
notes: Guards against the trap of trusting `nc` as proof the connection works. The skill is explicit: nc success != MongoDB responding. A zombie SSH session leaves the port open while nothing answers; verification must happen at the protocol level, and the fix is re-establishing the tunnel.
